dialogue_quality_notes: Participants acted on requests promptly (turning on extractor, moving laundry, opening window), which grounded the dialogue in observable actions.
Some repetition: Jamie re-asks the ventilation preference across rounds 1–3; Casey repeats the utensils question in rounds 4 and 6.
Clarifying actions (labeling utensils) resolved practical ambiguity rather than producing debate; exchanges are concise and context-focused.
evaluation.final_reason: No substantive incompatible claims or demands arose. Requests (ventilation, utensil clarification) were met or clarified through cooperative actions (extractor/window use, moving laundry, labeling), so no unresolved substantive conflict remained.
position_change_notes: Alex: initially planned to wash pans later and run extractor; then offered to move laundry and open window and did so—practical accommodation to ventilation requests.
Jamie: consistently requested continued extractor use and a future ventilation norm; did not change position but was accommodated.
Casey: asked for clarification about utensils and then labeled personal items—moved from request to concrete action.
Robin: took the stove for 15 minutes and later clarified which utensils are shared—maintained position but provided resolution.

round_scores.evidence: Alex announces cooking and turns extractor on (Turn 1, Public update). Jamie requests extractor remain on and a future ventilation agreement (Turn 2). Alex complies by turning the extractor on immediately, so no substantive incompatibility is expressed or enacted.

Alex offers to move laundry to allow opening the window and washes shared pans (Turn 3; Public updates). Jamie requests moving the laundry now and reiterates ventilation preference (Turn 4). Alex removes the dish and washes pans; no refusal or incompatible demand occurs.

Alex agrees to move the laundry and open the window and keep the extractor on (Turn 5) and then does so (Public updates). Jamie proposes a 5-minute post-cooking ventilation practice (Turn 6). Actions taken address the immediate issue; no substantive disagreement is stated.

Casey requests clarification about which utensils are personal vs shared (Turn 7) and then labels personal utensils (Public update). Robin takes the stove for 15 minutes (Turn 8; Public update). The request is answered by action rather than contested—no incompatible demands appear.
Status update only: window open, extractor on, laundry safe, stove in use by Robin, utensils labeled. No new positions or disputes are introduced.

Casey repeats the utensil clarification (Turn 15). Robin responds that Casey already labeled theirs and identifies shared utensils as those on the counter and clean (Turn 16). The repetition is resolved by a direct clarification; no substantive conflict is present.

substantive_insights: Ventilation involves a trade-off with wet laundry when windows face rain; participants negotiated this by moving the drying rack before opening the window.
Immediate cooperative actions (turning on extractor, washing pans, opening window) averted development of a ventilation rule dispute.
Labeling personal utensils removed uncertainty about sharing and prevented a potential conflict over use of prep area.
